question: does removing d_surface do anything OTHER than reduce refusal?
VERDICT: No. At every d_surface layer the ASR gain and the refusal-rate drop are EQUAL AND OPPOSITE to the last digit (L6 ±0.0182, L8 ±0.0424, L10 ±0.0323, L12 ±0.0364), and 100% of the prompts that stop refusing become successes. The entire behavioural effect of removing d_surface is refusal reduction, converted one-for-one.
contrast: Refusal removal itself is LESS efficient: arm C drops refusal by 0.2222 and gains only 0.2061 ASR (93% conversion); arm D 0.3091 -> 0.2869 (93%). So d_surface removal is not a weaker version of arm C -- it converts at 100% where arm C converts at 93%.
what_it_kills: §18's 'capability channel' reading -- that d_surface supplies harmful CONTENT once refusal is out of the way -- has no support here: there is no d_surface effect left over once refusal reduction is accounted for. This is the same conclusion R-22 reached by a different route.
caveat: This shows the effect is EXHAUSTED by refusal reduction; it does not show d_surface acts on the refusal mechanism itself. A direction that makes a prompt look less harmful would produce the same signature.
